name: Diana Jeudi
review:
**Verdict:** Friendly, service-oriented background but no visible mental health, behavioral health, or direct-care experience — worth a phone screen to gauge interest and trainability rather than a clear yes or no on paper.

**Strengths:** Steady front-desk/receptionist experience (Scruffy to Fluffy, Monster Mini Golf) showing reliability and customer-facing comfort; currently pursuing a degree at Broward College; open to references.

**Gaps:** [VERIFY] No behavioral health, youth work, or clinical/technician experience anywhere in her history; Spanish listed as Basic only; compensation expectation ($16/hr) is on the low end, unclear if that matches this role's actual pay band.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) What draws you to working with adolescents in a mental health technician role specifically? 2) Have you had any experience — paid or volunteer — supervising, supporting, or de-escalating youth in a group setting?

**Recommendation:** Hold for phone screen — no hard disqualifiers, but background is a stretch. Flagging rather than deciding since I don't have this role's specific hiring guide loaded this session.

name: Brisa Sastre
review:
**Verdict:** Retail/sales background (Nike) with fluent Spanish and stated interest in moving into social work — no direct behavioral health or youth-facing experience yet, but she's already at Phone Screen so someone on the team saw potential.

**Strengths:** Fluent/bilingual Spanish; explicitly stated goal of transitioning into the social work field; customer-facing experience with teamwork and goal-orientation.

**Gaps:** [VERIFY] No listed education, certifications, or prior direct-care/youth work experience; no work history beyond the Nike role provided in this pull — resume should be checked for anything not captured in the questionnaire.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) What's motivating your move from retail into social work / adolescent mental health work? 2) Any coursework, volunteering, or informal experience working with teens or in behavioral health settings?

**Recommendation:** Hold — already in your Phone Screen pipeline, so this is just an AI gut-check, not a new decision. No red flags found.

name: EDRIC WELDON
review:
**Verdict:** Strong athletic/coaching background and clear enthusiasm for working with youth, but no operations-management, supervisory, or behavioral-health experience — a stretch for a Services Manager title specifically.

**Strengths:** Sports Performance Intern and NCAA Division I athlete with real experience coaching/motivating younger athletes; comfortable with structure, discipline, and youth mentorship; available for both shift options; open to references.

**Gaps:** [VERIFY] Self-reported "Less than 1 year" of behavioral health/healthcare/adolescent-services experience and "experience with a different age group" (not the 13-17 target range) on his own questionnaire; has never directly supervised staff ("None"); most recent job (plumbing apprentice) has no overlap with this role at all; Spanish is Basic only.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) This role is a Manager position — can you walk me through any experience you've had managing people, schedules, or day-to-day operations, even informally? 2) You noted your youth experience is with a different age group — tell me more about that and how it'd translate to working with 13-17 year olds.

**Recommendation:** Hold — genuinely borderline on paper. His own answers (limited BH exposure, no direct supervisory experience, different age group) suggest this may be a stretch for a Manager-level role, but the coaching background is a real asset. Flagging for your read rather than deciding since I don't have this role's hiring guide loaded this session.

name: Edwin Cordon
review:
**Verdict:** Solid HR/administrative generalist with one part-time recruiting internship — meets the bar on recruiting exposure, though it's thin and mostly HR-ops rather than full-cycle recruiting.

**Strengths:** Bilingual (fluent Spanish); actual "HR Recruitment Intern" experience at FindMe (candidate tracking, scheduling, onboarding prep, workflow coordination); strong, steady HR/ops track record across multiple employers (Tri County Sweeping, Fanatics, BrightStar Credit Union); business administration degree.

**Gaps:** The recruiting internship was part-time/remote and relatively brief (6 months); most of his experience is HR operations and administration rather than sourcing/recruiting; no healthcare or behavioral health industry exposure specifically.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) Walk me through your day-to-day at FindMe — how much of that role was actual candidate sourcing and outreach versus administrative support? 2) What interests you about recruiting specifically for behavioral health roles?

**Recommendation:** Advance to phone screen — meets the recruiting-exposure bar, bilingual is a plus for this role.

name: Renae Marston
review:
**Verdict:** No recruiting experience anywhere in her background — healthcare exposure (Memorial Healthcare System) but nothing sourcing- or hiring-related. Doesn't meet the recruiting-exposure bar we've been applying to this role.

**Strengths:** Healthcare industry familiarity (Memorial Healthcare System); psychology coursework at Broward College.

**Gaps:** No work history details provided; no recruiting, HR, or talent acquisition experience of any kind; Spanish is Basic only; compensation expectation ($22/hr) suggests she may be earlier-career.

**Phone screen questions:** N/A — recommending disqualify per the recruiting-exposure requirement.

**Recommendation:** Disqualify — no recruiting exposure, per your standing instruction that this is a must-have for the Behavioral Health Recruiter role. Note: she was already manually advanced to Video Screen before this review — you confirmed disqualifying anyway.

name: Aileen Carmona
review:
**Verdict:** Strong, credentialed mental health counseling background (Master's in Clinical Mental Health, multiple counselor roles) but zero recruiting or talent acquisition experience — doesn't meet the recruiting-exposure requirement for this role.

**Strengths:** Master's degree in Education & Clinical Mental Health Counseling; extensive direct clinical experience (residential mental health counselor, school counselor intern, youth shelter counselor); fluent/bilingual Spanish; strong writing and clear commitment to the mental health field.

**Gaps:** No recruiting, HR, or talent acquisition experience anywhere in her history — her whole background is clinical/counseling, not sourcing or hiring; this looks like a strong candidate for a clinical role, just not this recruiting-titled one.

**Phone screen questions:** N/A — recommending disqualify per the recruiting-exposure requirement.

**Recommendation:** Disqualify from Behavioral Health Recruiter per the recruiting-exposure rule — but worth flagging: her clinical background could be a strong fit for a counseling/clinical role instead, if you have one open. Note: same name coincidentally appears on the Adolescent Services Manager pipeline from an earlier batch — worth confirming if that's her too or a different Aileen Carmona.

name: NICOLE INTRANOVA
review:
**Verdict:** Strong direct fit — actual Talent Acquisition Specialist and Field Recruiter titles with multi-market full-cycle recruiting experience.

**Strengths:** Current HR Talent Acquisition Specialist (GLOSSLAB) running full-cycle recruiting across nine markets; prior Field Recruiter role (Edison Home Health Care) with community/job-fair outreach experience directly relevant to healthcare recruiting; fluent/bilingual Spanish; English Literature degree suggests strong writing/communication skills.

**Gaps:** No behavioral-health-specific recruiting experience listed (mostly retail/home health/banking); compensation ask ($25/hr) should be confirmed against the role's actual band.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) Tell me about your sourcing strategy at GLOSSLAB — what channels and tools have worked best for you? 2) What interests you about moving into behavioral health recruiting specifically?

**Recommendation:** Advance — one of the strongest fits in this batch on paper.

name: Nicolette Rose
review:
**Verdict:** Strong fit — explicitly titled "Full Cycle Recruiting Specialist" with 10+ years spanning healthcare, education, and talent acquisition.

**Strengths:** Current Full Cycle Recruiting Specialist (Kelly Education); healthcare environmental services background (Memorial Regional Hospital) adds industry familiarity; core qualifications list explicitly includes full-cycle recruitment, candidate sourcing, interview coordination, and onboarding.

**Gaps:** Spanish is Basic only; her recruiting title is combined with a substitute-teaching role, so it's worth confirming how much of her time was actually spent recruiting versus teaching.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) Can you break down your Kelly Education role — how much of it was recruiting versus classroom substitute work? 2) What healthcare recruiting experience do you have beyond the environmental services role at Memorial Regional?

**Recommendation:** Advance — clear recruiting title and healthcare exposure make her a strong candidate for a phone screen.

name: Anthony Perdigao
review:
**Verdict:** Long track record of hiring and staff development in hospitality/senior living, but no formal recruiting title — hiring was a component of broader operations/management roles, not his core function.

**Strengths:** Current Staff Development Manager (Erickson Senior Living) explicitly listing "recruiting, hiring, development of all staff" as a responsibility; long, stable management career (10+ years) with consistent staff training and hiring components across multiple employers.

**Gaps:** [VERIFY] Recruiting was always a side responsibility within a broader GM/manager role, never his primary function or title; no healthcare/behavioral-health-specific recruiting; Spanish is Conversational only.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) Of your day-to-day at Erickson Senior Living, roughly what share of your time is spent actively recruiting and hiring versus operations/training? 2) What's drawing you to move into a dedicated recruiting role after a management career?

**Recommendation:** Hold for phone screen — genuine hiring exposure but not a dedicated recruiter background. Borderline enough that I'd rather you weigh in than auto-advance or disqualify.

name: Manuchka Joseph
review:
**Verdict:** Strong fit — current Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist with a long, varied career touching recruiting, HR, and social-services case management.

**Strengths:** Current Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist (High Volume Workforce and Operations Staffing) with federal contractor recruiting experience; prior Human Service Coordinator role partnering directly with recruiters and hiring managers on talent acquisition strategy; additional background in child welfare/protective services case management, which could be a real asset for a behavioral-health-adjacent org.

**Gaps:** No education listed in this pull [VERIFY]; Spanish is Basic only; compensation ask ($25/hr) should be checked against the role's band.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) Tell me about your current full-cycle recruiting process at your present role — sourcing, screening, closing. 2) How do you think your social-services background (Child Advocate, Adult Protective Investigator) would translate to recruiting for behavioral health roles?

**Recommendation:** Advance — clear recruiting title plus relevant human-services background make this a strong candidate.

name: Charles M
review:
**Verdict:** Strong fit — explicitly describes 8+ years of healthcare recruiting and operations management, with a prior Program Manager role doing full-cycle clinical staffing.

**Strengths:** Program Manager (HealthTrust Workforce Solutions) managing full-cycle international clinical staffing and recruitment, partnering with hospital hiring managers; healthcare compliance background (HIPAA, EMTALA, AHCA training programs); bachelor's degree.

**Gaps:** Spanish is Basic only; current role (Lead Patient Financial Associate) is not a recruiting title, so his most recent day-to-day is finance-adjacent rather than active recruiting — worth confirming recency of his recruiting experience.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) It looks like your most recent role has been more finance/operations-focused — how recent is your hands-on recruiting experience? 2) Walk me through a full-cycle clinical placement you managed at HealthTrust.

**Recommendation:** Advance — strong healthcare recruiting background, worth confirming recency in the phone screen.

name: Vita Dellegrazie
review:
**Verdict:** Long, accomplished management career in spa/wellness and financial aid — but no recruiting title or dedicated talent-acquisition experience anywhere. Doesn't meet the recruiting-exposure bar.

**Strengths:** Extensive people-management experience (teams of 10+), interviewing and hiring were part of several roles (European Wax Center, Bliss Spa, spa management roles); strong operational and customer-relationship skills.

**Gaps:** No recruiting or talent-acquisition title or function anywhere in her career; hiring was a small piece of broader spa/retail operations management, not her core responsibility; Spanish is Basic only; background has no connection to healthcare or behavioral health.

**Phone screen questions:** N/A — recommending disqualify per the recruiting-exposure requirement.

**Recommendation:** Disqualify — no recruiting exposure, per your standing rule for this role. Note: she was already manually advanced to Video Screen before this review — you confirmed disqualifying anyway.

name: Fanny Salgado
review:
**Verdict:** Excellent fit — current HealthCare Recruiter with a strong, specific track record in full-cycle healthcare/clinical recruiting.

**Strengths:** Current HealthCare Recruiter (MPLT Healthcare) doing full-cycle locum tenens recruiting for Advanced Practice Providers; multiple prior Regional/Associate Recruiter roles (Health Trust Workforce Solutions) with concrete sourcing and placement metrics (20+ facility partnerships, 40-50 submissions/month); fluent/bilingual Spanish.

**Gaps:** Her healthcare recruiting experience is specifically in locum tenens/nursing placement rather than behavioral health, and she states she's looking to transition into HR Generalist/Coordinator work — worth confirming she's genuinely interested in staying in a recruiting-titled role rather than using it as a stepping stone to HR.

**Phone screen questions:** 1) You mentioned wanting to transition into HR Generalist/Coordinator work — how does a dedicated Behavioral Health Recruiter role fit into that goal? 2) What's your process for sourcing and vetting healthcare candidates at MPLT?

**Recommendation:** Advance — strongest recruiting background in this batch; just confirm her career-direction fit in the screen.
